question.text: An air bubble of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> rises steadily through a solution of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1750</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> at the rate of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>35</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The co-efficient of viscosity of the solution (neglect density of air) is ________ Pas (given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>).

solution.text:
The bubble is moving with a constant velocity so the net force acting on the body is zero.

Stokes' law defines the drag force which is given by F=6πηrv

The buoyant force is given by B=Vρg=43πr3ρg

Hence, it can be written that

43πr3ρg=6πηrv⇒η=2r2ρg9v=2×3×10-32×1750×109×0.35×10-2=10 Pas
